title: How to create a database in Notion on Mac: step by step for the desktop app
metaTitle: How to Create a Database in Notion on Mac (Step by Step)
description: Learn how to create a database in Notion on Mac. Start a new page, choose Table or type /database, then add properties, views, and filters in the desktop app.

intro: To create a database in Notion on Mac, open the desktop app, press ⌘N for a new page, then choose ••• → Table under Get started with. Give it a name, add properties, and build views from inside the database.
tldr: Open the Notion desktop app, press ⌘N, and choose ••• → Table under Get started with.
Or type /database in a page you already have to put a database inside it.
A full-page database lives in the sidebar. An inline database sits inside another page.
Add properties with Edit property → Change type, and add views with + next to the database name.
If you can see a database but can't add pages, check your permission level before you retry.

blocks.text: A Notion database is a table of pages. Each row is a page, and each column is a property such as a status, a date, or a number. You can build one for a reading list, a client tracker, or a recipe box. This guide covers the path that works in the Notion desktop app on a Mac, and it notes where Notion's own help center is silent.
What you need before you start

The Notion desktop app runs on macOS 13 or later. Notion's system requirements page lists macOS 13 or above and advises running the latest macOS for the best experience. It doesn't list RAM or disk requirements, so check those yourself if your Mac is older.

Notion publishes three Mac builds: Intel (x64), Apple silicon (arm64), and Universal. The Universal build works on both chip types, but its installer is much larger. Each build downloads from its own link, and the app installs to /Applications by default. It updates itself with each new release.

If the app isn't installed yet, follow [how to install the desktop app on Mac](/how-to/install-the-desktop-app-in-notion). Then sign in to your workspace. You need an account that can create pages in that workspace, which matters later when permissions come up.
Start from a new page with ⌘N

Press ⌘N while the desktop app is in front. Notion creates a new page. Under Get started with, you'll see a few choices. The help center lists ••• → Table, Build with AI, suggested templates, and More templates. Pick Table when you want a blank grid. Pick a template when you want a head start.

blocks.caption: Options under Get started with, as described in Notion's help center
rows: A blank database, ready for your own properties.
Opens Suggested and More templates, then select Get started.
Notion's AI builds a database from your description. The AI can't edit existing databases, add pages, or build automations, forms, charts, or templates.
Opens more templates beyond the suggested ones.

blocks.text: Build with AI is free on Business and Enterprise plans. On other plans it uses workspace credits, including complimentary credits. Check the pricing page before you rely on it for a team workspace.
Type /database in a page you already have

Open an existing page, click an empty line, and type /database. Press Return. This works well when you already have notes, a project brief, or a meeting page, and you want the database to sit inside it. Notion's keyboard shortcuts page lists no shortcut for creating a database. The slash command is the quickest route in an existing page.
Full-page or inline: where the database lives

A database you create from a new page is a full-page database. It appears in the sidebar like any other page. To make a database inline, drag it under another page, open that page, and choose Turn into inline from the ⋮⋮ menu. An inline database sits inside the page, among your text and other blocks. You can expand an inline database to a full page with ⤡.
Pick full-page when the database is the thing you open every day. Pick inline when the database supports a longer page, such as a project brief with a task list at the bottom.
Add properties, the columns of your database

Properties are the columns. Click a property name, then choose Edit property → Change type to see every property type. Pick the type before you fill in rows, so you don't have to rebuild the column later. Use Edit property → Add an option to add choices for a property that offers them.
A worked example: a reading list

Say you're building a reading list for a book club. The Title column is already there. Add a Status property with choices, then add three options: To read, Reading, and Done. Add a Rating property with a number type. Add a Finished property with a date type for the day you close the book.

items: Title: the name of each book. This column is already there.
Status: a choice property with To read, Reading, and Done.
Rating: a number you fill in after you finish the book.
Finished: a date for the day you close the book.

blocks.text: Use the + button to the right of an existing property to add the next one. A short list of well-chosen columns beats a long list you never fill in.
Add views, filters, and sorts

A view is a way of looking at the same rows. Click + next to the database name and choose Board to see the reading list as cards grouped by status. Each view keeps its own filters and sorts. Open the settings menu at the top of the database to set them.

Use a filter to hide finished books in one view while another view shows everything. Changes to one view don't reset the others. This is how you can keep a Board for planning and a Table for logging, both on the same data.
Lock views and duplicate without breaking the setup

Open ••• at the top right to lock views. Locking blocks changes to properties and views, but not to the data in rows. Anyone with editing access can switch the lock on or off. A lock keeps the layout steady. It doesn't protect the content.

To duplicate an inline database, use the ⋮⋮ menu. For a full-page database, use the ••• menu at the top right. Notion asks whether you want to copy with or without content. Pick without content when you want the structure and a fresh start.
Why you can't add pages to a database you can see

Database permissions work separately from page permissions. Notion's sharing help describes a person with access to only one task page who can't create new pages in the database. Notion's suggested workaround is a form. The Can create permission lets people add pages without seeing the other content. The sharing help page says it's available on Business and Enterprise plans.

Notion added Can create in its March 5, 2026 release. The release note doesn't mention Mac support or which plans include it. If the option is missing on your Mac, check your plan and update the app before you assume it's broken.

blocks.text: What a database costs before you build

Databases are included in Notion's Free plan, including custom properties. Solo Free users can add unlimited pages and blocks. Free workspaces with several members have a block limit, but the pricing page doesn't state the number. Check the pricing page before you plan a team rollout.

Notion's pricing page lists Custom Agents as free to try, then $10 per 1,000 monthly Notion credits. Those credits are separate from the database itself. Plan for them only if you plan to use Notion's AI features.
Common mistakes people make

items: Choosing Database when you wanted Table. Database opens templates first, so a blank grid takes one extra step.
Dragging a database to the wrong place. A full-page database goes to the sidebar. An inline one lives inside the page you dragged it under.
Filtering a view and thinking the whole database changed. Filters belong to the view where you set them.
Locking views and assuming the data is safe. Locking views doesn't stop row edits.
Changing a property type after you fill in rows. Pick the type first.
Pressing ⌘N in a browser tab. The help center documents this shortcut for the desktop app only.

blocks.text: Where Notion's help center stops

Notion's help describes database steps as clicks on the page, such as ••• → Table. It doesn't list a File, Edit, or View menu path in the Mac menu bar. The steps above use the labels you see on the page. The database help pages show no version or date, so these steps reflect the help center as of November 7, 2026.

Notion's database steps had no change in 2026, according to the help center. Desktop build numbers vary across third-party sites, so don't rely on a build number to find the right menu. If a label on your screen differs from this guide, trust the screen.
What to do next

Once the database exists, add a few real rows and check the view you'll use each day. If the app won't open on an older Mac, read [the application not supported fix](/how-to/fix-the-application-not-supported-error-in-notion). If you're still choosing a Mac setup, [check the system requirements](/how-to/check-system-requirements-in-notion) first.

faq.question: Can I create a database in Notion on Mac without the desktop app?
faq.answer: Yes. Notion's help covers database creation for the web and desktop together, and the steps are much the same. Only ⌘N is documented for the desktop app, so in a browser create a page first, then choose Table or type /database.

faq.question: What is the difference between Table and Database under Get started with?
faq.answer: Table gives you a blank database to build from scratch. Database opens templates, either Suggested templates or More templates. Choose one, then select Get started.

faq.question: Why can't I add pages to a database I can see?
faq.answer: Page-level access to a single page doesn't let you add pages to the database. Notion suggests a form as a workaround. On Business and Enterprise plans, the Can create permission lets people add new pages.

faq.question: Does creating a database in Notion cost money?
faq.answer: Databases are included in Notion's Free plan. Solo Free users can add unlimited pages and blocks. AI-built databases are free on Business and Enterprise plans, and other plans use workspace credits.

faq.question: How do I turn a full-page database into an inline database?
faq.answer: Drag the database under another page in the sidebar, open that page, and choose Turn into inline from the ⋮⋮ menu. The database then sits inside that page.

faq.question: Why can't I edit my database even though I'm in it?
faq.answer: Locked views or view-only access will block edits. Check the ••• menu at the top right for a lock. Locking stops property and view changes, but not data changes, and anyone with editing access can toggle it.

appliesTo: Notion desktop app for Mac, macOS 13 or later
requirements: Notion desktop app installed on macOS 13 or later
A Notion account that can create pages in the workspace

steps.name: Open the Notion desktop app
steps.text: Open Notion from your Applications folder or the Dock. If you don't have the desktop app yet, install it first, because ⌘N works only in the desktop app. The desktop app needs macOS 13 or later.

steps.name: Create a new page
steps.text: Press ⌘N. Notion's help center says this shortcut creates a new page in the desktop app. A new page opens with the Get started with options.
steps.tip: If nothing happens, click inside the Notion window first so it has keyboard focus.

steps.name: Choose Table under Get started with
steps.text: On the new page, find the Get started with section. Click ••• and choose Table. Notion creates a blank database on the page.
steps.tip: Choose Database instead if you want a template. It opens Suggested and More templates before anything else.

steps.name: Name the database
steps.text: Click the title at the top of the page and type a name, such as Reading list. A full-page database appears in the sidebar under that name, like any other page.

steps.name: Add and edit properties
steps.text: Click a property name, then choose Edit property → Change type to see every property type. Use the + button to the right of a property to add another one. For choices, use Edit property → Add an option.
steps.tip: Pick each property type before you fill in rows, so you don't have to redo the column.

steps.name: Add a view
steps.text: Click + next to the database name and choose a layout such as Board. Each view has its own filters and sorts, so a new view doesn't change the first one.

steps.name: Filter and sort the view
steps.text: Open the settings menu at the top of the database. Set your filters and sorts there. They apply to the view you're in, not to every view.

steps.name: Lock views if others edit
steps.text: Open ••• at the top right and choose Lock views when you want the layout to stay put. Locking blocks changes to properties and views, but not to the data in rows. Anyone with editing access can toggle it.
steps.tip: Tell your team before you lock. Locking is a layout control, not a content control.

troubleshooting.fix: Check that you're in the desktop app, not a browser tab. Notion's help documents ⌘N for the desktop app only. Click inside the Notion window and try again.

troubleshooting.problem: The desktop app won't open on my Mac
troubleshooting.fix: Check your macOS version first. Notion's desktop app needs macOS 13 or above. On an older Mac you may see an application not supported error, so read the fix page linked above.

troubleshooting.problem: I can't find the database after I made it
troubleshooting.fix: A full-page database appears in the sidebar. An inline database sits inside the page you dragged it under. Press ⌘K to search for it by name.

troubleshooting.problem: I can't add pages to the database
troubleshooting.fix: Page-level access to one page doesn't allow new pages in the database. Ask the owner for Can create on Business or Enterprise, or use a form.

troubleshooting.problem: I can see the database but can't edit views or properties
troubleshooting.fix: Check the ••• menu at the top right for Lock views. You may also have view-only access, so ask the owner for editing access.
